stories.headline: Egypt, Pakistan, and Turkey Submit 45-Day Ceasefire Proposal to Iran and US

key_facts.fact: Egyptian, Pakistani, and Turkish mediators sent Iran and the US a proposal calling for a 45-day ceasefire and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, submitted late Sunday to Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff.
key_facts.excerpt: Egyptian, Pakistani and Turkish mediators have sent Iran and the U.S. a proposal calling for a 45-day ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: The framework, drafted by Pakistan and tentatively dubbed the 'Islamabad Agreement,' envisions a 15- to 20-day window to finalize a broader regional settlement after an immediate ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: The framework—drafted by Pakistan—was exchanged overnight with both Tehran and Washington, describing a phased approach beginning with an immediate ceasefire followed by a comprehensive agreement

key_facts.fact: The plan includes Iranian commitments to abandon pursuit of nuclear weapons in exchange for sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets, with Pakistan serving as the sole communication channel.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan shares ceasefire framework to end US-Iran war

key_facts.fact: Iran rejected the idea of reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a temporary ceasefire, with a senior official telling Reuters that Tehran views Washington as lacking readiness for a permanent ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a 'temporary ceasefire'

key_facts.fact: Neither Iran nor the US had formally responded to the proposal as of Sunday night. Pakistani officials said ceasefire efforts were 'at an advanced stage' but faced 'several spoilers and detractors.'
key_facts.excerpt: Neither Iran nor the U.S. had responded to the proposal

stories.headline: Israel Strikes Iran's South Pars Petrochemical Complex, Kills Two IRGC Commanders

key_facts.fact: Israel struck a petrochemical plant at Iran's South Pars natural gas field on Monday April 6, which Israel's defense minister described as 'a powerful strike on the largest petrochemical facility in Iran, located in Asaluyeh.'
key_facts.excerpt: a powerful strike on the largest petrochemical facility in Iran, located in Asaluyeh

key_facts.fact: The strike killed Maj. Gen. Majid Khademi, head of intelligence for Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and Asghar Bakeri, leader of the Revolutionary Guard's undercover unit in the Quds Force.
key_facts.excerpt: Maj. Gen. Majid Khademi (head of intelligence for Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard) ... Asghar Bakeri (leader of the Revolutionary Guard's undercover unit in the Quds Force)

key_facts.fact: Israel's defense minister said the facility was 'responsible for about 50% of the country's petrochemical production' and the strike aimed at eliminating a major revenue source for Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: a central target responsible for about 50% of the country's petrochemical production

key_facts.fact: Israel's defense minister vowed to continue targeting top-ranking Iranian officials, saying 'Iran's leaders live with a sense of being targeted. We will continue to hunt them down one by one.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's leaders live with a sense of being targeted. We will continue to hunt them down one by one.

key_facts.fact: The strike came just as mediators floated a new 45-day ceasefire proposal, casting doubt on its viability. Explosions in Tehran and low-flying jets were heard for hours afterward.
key_facts.excerpt: Explosions in Tehran and low-flying jets heard for hours following the attacks

stories.headline: Trump Threatens to Destroy Iran's Power Plants and Bridges by Tuesday

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on social media: 'Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one, in Iran. There will be nothing like it!!!' followed by 'Open the F****** Strait, you crazy b******, or you'll be living in Hell.'
key_facts.excerpt: Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one, in Iran. There will be nothing like it!!!

key_facts.fact: Trump set the deadline for 8 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday (0100 GMT Wednesday), telling the Wall Street Journal the US will destroy 'every power plant' in Iran if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump again threatens to bomb Iran's power plants if Strait of Hormuz is not reopened

key_facts.fact: Iran dismissed the threats as desperation. Deputy communications officer Seyyed Mehdi Tabatabaei said the US had 'resorted to obscenities and nonsense out of sheer desperation and anger.'
key_facts.excerpt: resorted to obscenities and nonsense out of sheer desperation and anger

key_facts.fact: Trump has issued similar ultimatums before that he extended when mediators claimed progress, making it unclear whether he will follow through on this threat.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump having issued similar ultimatums before that he extended when mediators claimed progress

stories.headline: Iran Exempts Iraq from Hormuz Restrictions; First Major Crude Tanker Transits Strait

key_facts.fact: Iran's military declared Iraq exempt from Strait of Hormuz restrictions, saying limitations would only apply to 'enemy countries' and 'Brotherly Iraq is exempt from any restrictions we have imposed on the Strait of Hormuz.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran says Iraqi ships are allowed to use Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: The Ocean Thunder, an Iraqi-flagged tanker loaded with roughly 1 million barrels of Basrah Heavy crude, successfully transited the Strait on April 5, tracked passing close to the Iranian coastline.
key_facts.excerpt: Iraqi Oil Tanker Safely Navigates Strait of Hormuz After Iran Grants Transit Exemption

key_facts.fact: Data from LSEG and Kpler confirmed the tanker is en route to Pengerang, Malaysia, for a Petronas-chartered delivery expected in mid-April.
key_facts.excerpt: Tanker loaded with Iraqi crude passes through Hormuz, shipping data shows

key_facts.fact: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is still down more than 90% from pre-war levels, with 53 transits last week—the most since the war began—up from 36 the previous week.
key_facts.excerpt: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is still down more than 90% from pre-war levels, with 53 transits through the strait last week, the most since the war began

key_facts.fact: Iraq is the world's sixth-largest oil producer and second-largest in OPEC, accounting for about 4% of global supply, with oil revenues making up around 90% of its state budget.
key_facts.excerpt: Iraq is the world's sixth-largest oil producer and the second-largest in OPEC

stories.headline: Iranian Drone Strikes Damage Kuwait Power Plants and Knock Desalination Offline

key_facts.fact: Iranian drones and missiles struck multiple sites in Kuwait on April 5, including the Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex and two power and water desalination plants, causing significant material damage.
key_facts.excerpt: Kuwait's power, water plants damaged as Iran keeps attacking Gulf states

key_facts.fact: Kuwait's Ministry of Electricity reported the strikes took a water desalination station out of service and shut two electricity-generating units. Emergency plans were activated to ensure service continuity.
key_facts.excerpt: the strikes disabled a water desalination station, according to Kuwait's Ministry of Electricity

key_facts.fact: The Shuwaikh complex was evacuated after fires were reported at key oil and government facilities. No casualties were confirmed by Kuwaiti authorities.
key_facts.excerpt: No injuries were reported

key_facts.fact: Bahrain also experienced drone attacks causing fires at national oil company storage and a state-run petrochemical plant. The UAE responded to fires at a Ruwais petrochemical plant from intercepted debris, halting operations.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahrain experienced drone attacks causing fires at national oil company storage and a state-run petrochemical plant. The UAE responded to fires at a Ruwais petrochemical plant

key_facts.fact: The overall conflict death toll stands at over 1,900 killed in Iran, 1,400+ in Lebanon with over 1 million displaced, 20+ across Gulf states and the West Bank, 23 in Israel, and 13 US service members.
key_facts.excerpt: Over 1,900 killed in Iran; more than two dozen in Gulf states and West Bank; 19 in Israel; 13 U.S. service members; 1,400+ in Lebanon with over 1 million displaced

stories.headline: Oil Prices Swing Between $108-$114 on Trump Threats and Ceasefire Hopes

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 1.4% to $110.60 and US WTI crude rose 1.8% to $113.60 on Sunday after Trump threatened to strike Iranian energy facilities if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices rise as Trump warns Iran to open Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday or face 'hell'

key_facts.fact: Oil then switched from gains to losses as traders weighed a reported push for a ceasefire against the fresh Trump ultimatum. WTI dropped about 1% to $110.45 and Brent was little changed at $108.76.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices slide as Trump warns Iran to open Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday or face 'hell'

key_facts.fact: By early Asia trading on April 6, Brent crude was up 0.7% at $109.80 while US crude hovered near $111.62, reflecting ongoing uncertainty.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil Prices Volatile as Trump Threatens Iran Over Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Stock futures dropped alongside the oil price swings, with Fortune reporting fuel shortages mounting as Hormuz remains effectively closed to most shipping.
key_facts.excerpt: Stock market today: Oil rises and stock futures drop as Trump makes apocalyptic threats against Iran

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Course Correction, Crew Set for Historic Lunar Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Orion spacecraft completed a 17.5-second outbound correction burn at 11:03 p.m. EDT on April 5 to refine its trajectory toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: The outbound correction burn occurred at 11:03 p.m. EDT, lasting 17.5 seconds to refine Orion's trajectory toward the Moon

key_facts.fact: The crew entered the Moon's sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. EDT on April 6. The flyby window runs from 2:45-9:40 PM EDT April 6, with closest approach at 4,070 miles from the lunar surface at 7:02 p.m.
key_facts.excerpt: The crew enters the Moon's sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. on April 6

key_facts.fact: At 1:56 p.m. EDT April 6, the crew will surpass Apollo 13's record for humans' farthest distance from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,757 miles—4,105 miles farther than Apollo 13.
key_facts.excerpt: 1:56 p.m.: Crew surpasses Apollo 13's distance record from Earth

key_facts.fact: All four crew members—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—completed testing of the Orion Crew Survival System suits including pressurization, leak checks, and simulated seat entry.
key_facts.excerpt: putting on and pressurizing the suit, performing leak checks, simulating seat entry, and assessing mobility and their ability to eat and drink

key_facts.fact: NASA scientists identified about 35 geological features for the crew to observe during the flyby. The crew will work in pairs to photograph sites and describe them in real time to Mission Control.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA's Artemis II crew readies for Monday's lunar flyby

key_facts.fact: Orion will pass behind the Moon at 6:44 p.m. EDT, losing communications for approximately 40 minutes. 'Earthrise' and signal reacquisition are expected at 7:25 p.m.
key_facts.excerpt: 6:44 p.m.: Loss of communications as Orion passes behind the Moon (~40 minutes)

stories.headline: Spain's Xoople Raises $130M Series B to Build Earth-Mapping Satellite Constellation

key_facts.fact: Xoople closed a $130 million Series B led by Nazca Capital, with participation from MCH Private Equity, CDTI (a Spanish government-backed tech fund), Buenavista Equity Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst, bringing total funding to $225 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Xoople raises $130 million Series B to map the Earth for AI

key_facts.fact: Xoople is building a satellite constellation to collect precise Earth data for deep learning models, with sensors designed to collect data 'two orders of magnitude better than existing monitoring systems.'
key_facts.excerpt: a stream of data that is going to be two orders of magnitude better than existing monitoring systems

key_facts.fact: Xoople struck a deal with US space and defense contractor L3Harris Technologies to begin building sensors for its spacecraft, which will collect optical data.
key_facts.excerpt: a deal with L3Harris to build the sensors for Xoople's spacecraft

key_facts.fact: CEO Fabrizio Pirondini said the company is 'in unicorn territory' but declined to share the specific valuation. Xoople was founded in 2019 and has spent seven years developing its tech stack.

stories.headline: Drift Reveals $270M Crypto Exploit Was a Six-Month North Korean Intelligence Op

key_facts.fact: Drift Protocol, the largest decentralized perpetual futures exchange on Solana, revealed on April 5 that its $270M exploit on April 1 was a six-month intelligence operation by a North Korean state-affiliated group.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift says $270 million exploit was a six-month North Korean intelligence operation

key_facts.fact: The attackers first made contact at a major crypto conference around fall 2025, posing as a quantitative trading firm. They onboarded an Ecosystem Vault, deposited over $1 million of their own capital, and held multiple working sessions with contributors.
key_facts.excerpt: Attackers posed as a trading firm, met Drift contributors in person across multiple countries, deposited $1 million of their own capital

key_facts.fact: The attacker abused Solana's 'durable nonces' feature to pre-sign transactions that remained valid for over a week, then obtained two misleading approvals from Drift's five-member Security Council multisig to seize protocol control in minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Here is how Drift attackers drained more than $270 million using a Solana feature designed for convenience

key_facts.fact: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic flagged the exploit as consistent with previous DPRK-attributed operations based on on-chain behavior, laundering methodologies, and network-level indicators. Total DPRK crypto theft in 2026 exceeds $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol exploited for $286 million in suspected DPRK-linked attack

key_facts.fact: TRM Labs confirmed the attack represents the eighteenth DPRK-linked crypto operation tracked in 2026, making North Korea the most prolific state-sponsored crypto threat actor.
key_facts.excerpt: North Korean Hackers Attack Drift Protocol In USD 285 Million Heist

stories.headline: OpenAI Proposes Robot Taxes, Public Wealth Fund, 4-Day Workweek for AI Era

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First,' proposing policies for a world with AI superintelligence including a public wealth fund, taxes on automated labor, and a potential four-day workweek.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI calls for robot taxes, a public wealth fund, and a 4-day workweek to tackle AI disruption

key_facts.fact: The proposal calls for lawmakers and AI companies to jointly invest in a public wealth fund linked to the AI boom, with returns distributed directly to citizens.
key_facts.excerpt: a public wealth fund, which would see lawmakers and AI companies work together to invest in long-term assets linked to the AI boom, with returns distributed directly to citizens

key_facts.fact: OpenAI suggests actively measuring how AI affects wages and unemployment, and once 'these metrics exceed pre-defined thresholds,' offering workers increased unemployment benefits or job training.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI advocates electric grid, safety net spending in AI era

key_facts.fact: The document proposes incentivizing employers to experiment with four-day workweeks as a way to let workers share in AI-driven efficiency gains, as long as output doesn't fall.
key_facts.excerpt: incentivising employers to experiment with four-day work weeks, as long as workers' output doesn't fall

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman told Axios he feels 'urgency' about the power of coming AI models and called the proposals a 'New Deal for superintelligence' to 'wake up DC.'
key_facts.excerpt: @sama tells me he feels such URGENCY about the power of coming AI models that @OpenAI is unveiling a New Deal for superintelligence - ideas to wake up DC
